question: Compare the performance of product category X and category Y — why do they perform differently?
sql:
SELECT p.category, COUNT(oi.id) AS units_sold, ROUND(SUM(oi.sale_price), 2) AS revenue, ROUND(SUM(oi.sale_price - p.cost), 2) AS gross_profit, ROUND(AVG(oi.sale_price), 2) AS avg_price, ROUND(SAFE_DIVIDE(COUNTIF(oi.status = 'Returned'), COUNT(oi.id)) * 100, 1) AS return_rate_pct
FROM `bigquery-public-data.thelook_ecommerce.order_items` oi
JOIN `bigquery-public-data.thelook_ecommerce.products` p ON p.id = oi.product_id
WHERE p.category IN ('Jeans', 'Accessories')
  AND oi.status != 'Cancelled'
GROUP BY 1
report: For a 'why do they differ' question the analyst never stops at revenue: the comparison decomposes performance into volume (units), price point (avg price), profitability (gross profit using product cost) and quality signal (return rate). The narrative then attributes the gap to specific drivers, e.g. 'Jeans earn more per unit but Accessories win on volume; Jeans' higher return rate erodes its margin advantage'. A follow-up drill-down by brand within each category was included.
